fields.problem: The method that we propose in this paper addresses the general problem of meta-learning (Thrun & Pratt, 1998;
fields.method: We propose an algorithm for meta-learning that is model-agnostic, in the sense that it is compatible with any model trained with gradient descent and applicable to a variety of different learning problems, including classiﬁcation, regression, and reinforcement learning.
fields.limitation: We introduced a meta-learning method based on learning easily adaptable model parameters through gradient descent.
fields.takeaway: For example, a neural network might learn internal features that are broadly applicable to all tasks in p(T ), rather than a single individual task.

cards.title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

fields.problem: This survey focuses on Data Augmentation, a data-space solution to the problem of limited data.
fields.limitation: The paper concludes with a “Discussion” of the presented material, areas of “Future work”, and “Conclusion”.
fields.takeaway: Before discussing image augmentation techniques, it is useful to frame the context of the problem and consider what makes image recognition such a difficult task in the first place.

cards.title: A survey on Image Data Augmentation for Deep Learning

fields.problem: Few-shot or one-shot learning of classiﬁers requires a signiﬁcant inductive bias towards the type of task to be learned.
fields.method: In this paper, we propose UMTRA, an algorithm that performs unsupervised, model-agnostic meta-learning for classiﬁcation tasks.
fields.takeaway: Recently proposed model-agnostic meta-learning approaches [11, 31] can be applied to any differentiable network.

cards.title: Unsupervised Meta-Learning For Few-Shot Image Classification

fields.problem: In few-shot classiﬁcation, we are interested in learning algorithms that train a classiﬁer from only a handful of labeled examples.
fields.method: To address this paradigm, we propose novel extensions of Prototypical Networks (Snell et al., 2017) that are augmented with the ability to use unlabeled examples when producing prototypes.
fields.limitation: As future work, we are working on incorporating fast weights (Ba et al., 2016;
fields.takeaway: Indeed, much like a learning algorithm, the model must take in a set of labeled examples and produce a predictor that can be applied to new examples.

fields.problem: Medical datasets often have a skewed class distribution and a lack of high-quality annotated images.
fields.method: In this study, we present a few-shot learning approach for the classiﬁcation of ultrasound breast cancer images using meta-learning methods.
fields.takeaway: The methodology used in this study can be adapted to other datasets with similar problems.

cards.title: Few-shot classification of ultrasound breast cancer images using meta-learning algorithms

fields.problem: A more general approach to few-shot learning is by meta-learning, which trains a meta-learner from many related tasks to direct the learning of a learner for a new task, without relying on ad hoc knowledge about the problem.
fields.method: In this paper, we develop Meta-SGD, an SGD-like, easily trainable meta-learner that can initialize and adapt any differentiable learner in just one step, on both supervised learning and reinforcement learning.
fields.limitation: One important future work is large-scale meta-learning.
fields.takeaway: While these efforts can alleviate the issue of data scarcity to some extend, the way prior knowledge is used is speciﬁc and not generalizable.

cards.title: Meta-SGD: Learning to Learn Quickly for Few-Shot Learning
